title: Charred Capsicum Chicken Curry

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken thighs, roughly diced
water or chicken stock, to deglaze
brown or yellow onion, thinly sliced
canned crushed or diced tomatoes (2 cans)

steps: Mix the chicken with the Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, turmeric, lemon juice and plenty of salt. Set aside about 20 minutes.
Dice one onion small to medium and thinly slice the other. Slice the peppers into thin strips, then dice. Split the green chillies lengthways. Grate the garlic and ginger into a paste.

Heat a pan or pot over high heat until smoking hot and add 1 tbsp oil. Sear the chicken in batches, 2–3 minutes per side, about 6 minutes total, until browned but not cooked through. Move to a bowl and keep the fat in the pan.

Return the pan to medium-high heat. Add the diced onion, peppers and a pinch of salt, spread them out and leave 2–3 minutes until the edges char, then stir. Cook about 5 minutes total, turning the heat down if anything starts to burn.

Add the ¼ cup water or stock and scrape up the browned bits. Tip everything into a blender (or use an immersion blender) and pulse to a thick, wet, slightly grainy texture. Don't blend it to a paste; add a splash of water only if it won't turn over.
Wipe or reuse the pan over medium heat. Add 2 tbsp oil, the cumin seeds, the sliced onion and a pinch of salt. Cook about 8 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft and jammy with little colour.

Add the garlic-ginger paste and green chillies and cook 1 minute. Add the ground cumin, coriander, Kashmiri chilli powder and turmeric and cook about 20 seconds. Add the tomato paste and cook 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes and swirl ½ cup water around the cans. Stir in the blended charred vegetables, taste for salt and bring to a simmer. Cook on low for a while until thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the chicken and its resting juices and mix to coat. Simmer 8–10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (175°F / 79°C or more for thighs) and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the garam masala. Garnish with the crushed kasoori methi and chopped coriander. Taste for salt.

Portion into 5 containers (about 750 ml each) with rice. Cool slightly before putting the lids on. Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat in the microwave with a splash of stock or water.

subs.swap: breast, for leaner; simmer less so it doesn't dry out
leave out for a milder curry
skip; it only adds a slight bitterness
any veg that chars and blends well

notes: 2026-10-19 — Charred the veg and blended it coarse (thick, still a little grainy), simmered it with the tomatoes, then added the chicken. Really good. Might try charring the veg better.
